topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture themes, connects them to previous practical work, and outlines the learning objectives.

topics.label: Discovery of tumor viruses and cell transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays to measure cell transformation.

topics.label: Classification and mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define the major categories of cancer-associated mutations and illustrate their mechanistic actions using the retinoblastoma cell cycle pathway and p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the differences between sequence and chromosomal instability, detailing the DNA repair failures and mitotic defects that drive them.

topics.label: Multi-step tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how stepwise accumulation of mutations drives tumor evolution and how inherited gene defects accelerate cancer development.

topics.label: Lecture wrap-up and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture with a review of covered outcomes, reading suggestions, and a look ahead to the next session.
